Report that the source context is bounded and that speech/OS-input behavior is
separate from tree semantics. Default preparation is not default acceptance.

problems/P-199-Ladybug-prebuilt-metadata.filePath: problems/P-199 Ladybug prebuilt metadata writes a read-only registry.md
problems/P-199-Ladybug-prebuilt-metadata.title: P-199 — Ladybug prebuilt metadata writes a read-only registry
problems/P-199-Ladybug-prebuilt-metadata.content:
Status: open upstream; local normal-build retry works · Related: Rust Code Editor Accessibility and Cutover, P-144 bundled-symbol collisions
Problem
The installed lbug 0.21.0 build script correctly downloads a pinned prebuilt
archive into Cargo’s writable OUT_DIR/lbug-prebuilt/version-0.21.0-compat/lib.
Its scripts/download_lbug.sh then writes the default metadata file
<registry crate>/.cache/lbug-prebuilt.env. In this sandbox the registry is
read-only. The complete archive/header installation succeeds, but metadata
writing returns exit1. The caller reports a failed download and falls back to
building Ladybug from source, which fails here because cmake is absent.
Options





























approachprosconsARerun the identical normal build once after the archive is installedThe build script accepts the existing archive, including configured bundled-symbol localization; no registry/environment editsThe first build of another fresh OUT_DIR can fail againBGive downloader metadata a writable destination upstreamFixes fresh read-only-registry buildsRequires an upstream change or reviewed dependency patchCBuild Ladybug from sourceAvoids the prebuilt downloaderNeeds CMake/toolchain support and additional build cost
Measurements
NEXT-5’s actual desktop phase failed after 1108.119s, exit101, max
compiler/linker RSS 2566292KiB. It includes native DuckDB/RocksDB and Rust
dependency compilation, so that total is not Ladybug-only time. The downloader
installed the pinned archive successfully before the env-file error. Report:
target/next5-build-cost.json; complete diagnostic
target/next5-build-cost-logs/desktop_release.log.
The unchanged retry uses the same worktree target, release profile, jobs2,
locked/offline command and ordinary native environment (DOCS_RS unset).
try_download_prebuilt_lbug immediately accepts the now-existing archive, then
use_prebuilt_lbug applies LBUG_LOCALIZE_BUNDLED_SYMBOLS=1 as configured.
Retry evidence is kept separately in target/next5-desktop-retry.json and
target/next5-desktop-retry.log, not substituted for the failed phase.
Decision
Use A for this measurement and leave B open. Do not change registry source or
permissions, install tools or change production dependencies. Record the failed
initial phase, the retry’s different cache state and both elapsed times. The
fixture and artifact results are persisted before the optional product phase.
Lesson
A successful archive download can still be reported as failure by a later
metadata write. Read the complete build-script output before installing a source
build toolchain. Reuse the normal prebuilt path: linking a raw archive through
LBUG_LIBRARY_DIR/LBUG_INCLUDE_DIR skips this crate’s bundled-symbol localization
and can reintroduce the collisions documented in P-144.

problems/P-200-Lazy-syntactic-content-id.title: P-200 — Lazy syntactic content identities
problems/P-200-Lazy-syntactic-content-id.content:
Status: resolved for the experimental v1 contract, 2026-10-16 · Related: Code Graph Schema, Indexing, ADR-0026 Memory and the store
Problem
Location ids intentionally change on rename/move and cannot recognize structurally unchanged definitions. A content hash must exclude trivia/local names but keep observable spelling, propagate dependency changes and handle recursion without depending on source order. Eagerly hashing every indexed definition would violate the lazy-work requirement.
Options





























approachprosconsAhash raw definition bytessimplerenames/comments/moves are not handled correctly; dependencies are absentBversioned syntax normalization with explicit requests and bounded SCC hashingmeets the fixture contract without running codeconservative syntax support and same-file resolutionCcomplete compiler-backed semantic identitiesstronger semantic coveragerequires L3 frontends, external dependencies and dispatch rules
Measurements
The v1 three-language fixtures verify rename/move/trivia invariance, observable spelling, body/dependency changes, recursive components, stable unresolved paths, lazy persistent caching and freshness. Cache tests cover byte-budget eviction and corrupt/versioned records; integration tests force a concurrent refresh and malformed/deep/oversized input. Exact final command results are recorded in the Codex handoff; no throughput or semantic-proof claim is made.
Decision
B, behind the default-off content-ids Cargo feature. Keep location ids and source truth unchanged. Return typed errors for unsupported binding scopes rather than inventing identities. Store full BLAKE3 digests beside content UUIDs. Explicitly preserve Python keyword-capable parameter names and define symmetric SCC members as equivalent rather than breaking ties by name or location. The versioned specification is in Code Graph Schema.
Lesson
An alpha-normalizer needs a binding model, not a textual identifier replacement. Optional doc-only syntax containers must disappear with their docs. Ordered-reference graph canonicalization needs a symmetry rule. Exact input freshness and atomic publication matter as much as hashing; caches are replaceable derived data, never authority.

problems/P-202-Lossless-edits-must-conse.filePath: problems/P-202 Lossless edits must conserve syntax tokens.md
problems/P-202-Lossless-edits-must-conse.title: P-202 — Lossless edits must conserve syntax tokens
problems/P-202-Lossless-edits-must-conse.content:
Status: resolved in the default-off WP-67 foundation, 2026-10-16 · Related: Rust Lossless Syntax and Patches, ADR-0028 Files or the graph
Problem
A function moved with an EOF // comment can swallow following code because it has no newline. The resulting text can parse without errors despite losing a function or another item. Parser success alone is not enough to validate a lossless move. Additionally, name probes accepted forbidden Rust declaration names, and a per-edit output-size check rejected valid backward moves whose final size was unchanged.
Options





























approachprosconsAaccept any error-free parsesimplecan silently lose syntax tokensBinvent newlines/formatting at insertionoften repairs the parsechanges bytes and hides the ownership decisionCreparse, conserve function count and move token inventory, reject unsafe placementspreserves the exact edit contractsome placements require a later explicit separator operation
Measurements
The regression fixture moves a final function/comment before a first function with no leading newline; its error-free parse loses code. The corrected planner rejects it. Tests also cover CRLF block-comment terminators, protected file prefixes, stale plans, invalid UTF-8/overlap and a valid 512 KiB backward move. Final command results are recorded in the Codex handoff; no production graph action is enabled.
Decision
C. A planned move must retain every terminal token kind/spelling and the function count. Reject ambiguous placements rather than adding formatting. Name checks supplement the grammar with Rust’s reserved/raw identifier restrictions. Validate all edits and the final output size before constructing a result.
Lesson
Lossless printing preserves authored bytes; safe structural planning must also preserve the syntax those bytes express. Parsing, byte preservation and semantic refactoring are separate guarantees. This slice supplies pure plans, not a reference-aware Rename command.

problems/P-203-Nested-browser-fixtures-c.filePath: problems/P-203 Nested browser fixtures cannot load in rust-analyzer.md
problems/P-203-Nested-browser-fixtures-c.title: P-203 — Nested browser fixtures cannot load in rust-analyzer
problems/P-203-Nested-browser-fixtures-c.content:
Status: resolved, 2026-10-16 · Related: How to Write Tests, Rust Lossless Syntax and Patches
Problem
Running the ordinary browser fixture under this worktree’s target/wp67-e2e/m2root made lsp2 wait 120 seconds for diagnostics. cargo metadata --manifest-path …/m2root/Cargo.toml failed because Cargo discovered Moonkale’s parent workspace but the disposable package was not a member. The fixture worked outside the repository, hiding the problem.
Options





























approachprosconsAmove every fixture outside the repositoryavoids discoverycontradicts worktree-local artifact organization and needs more sandbox pathsBadd the disposable fixture to Moonkale’s workspacemetadata workschanges the product workspace for test dataCgive the generated fixture an empty [workspace] tablefixture is self-contained in any locationnone for this isolated test package
Measurements
The failed metadata command names both the fixture and parent Cargo.toml and recommends an empty [workspace]. The initial browser batch’s five non-LSP suites passed; lsp2 alone failed at server readiness. The corrected fixture and rerun are recorded in the Codex handoff; the failed first log is preserved.
Decision
C, in the shared fixture.sh template, before its fixture commit is created so run-all resets preserve it. No change to product workspace membership, runtime LSP handling, assertions or timeouts. Test builds remain in this worktree’s target directory.
Lesson
A disposable Rust project should declare its own workspace rather than depending on where the test runner puts it. Language-server readiness failures can originate in Cargo metadata rather than editor behavior.

problems/P-204-Structural-proposals-must.filePath: problems/P-204 Structural proposals must retain document identity.md
problems/P-204-Structural-proposals-must.title: P-204 — Structural proposals must retain document identity
problems/P-204-Structural-proposals-must.content:
Status: resolved · Related: Rust Lossless Syntax and Patches
Problem
A pure syntax plan guards source bytes but does not identify an editor session. Closing and reopening the same file, or editing and undoing back to the same bytes, must invalidate pending graph edits. A source can also be replaced or become read-only while a preview is open.
Options























approachprosconsAApply directly to Document text after checking its hashsimplebypasses history and session identityBCapture session/source identity, revision and version; use EditBatchexisting history and recoverable conflictsconsumer must explicitly replan
Measurements
ext-api/tests/document_proposals.rs uses a real Dioxus runtime and actual lossless Rust rename/move plans. It covers revision and close/reopen ABA, backing version, canonical drift, replaced sources, writable Files authority, Unicode/CRLF selection/history, invalid edits, bounds and retained dirty buffers after a version-conflicting save.
Decision
B: engine-neutral, bounded single-document proposals with immutable base/preview and typed conflicts. No silent rebase or autosave. Consumers retain failed proposals and explicitly capture/recompute or discard. Graph controls and visible conflict presentation remain the next slice.
Lesson
Exact input bytes, editor revision, session identity and backing source version answer different freshness questions. Check them together immediately before committing, without awaiting between checks and mutation.

problems/P-205-Graph-previews-must-rejec.filePath: problems/P-205 Graph previews must reject stale asynchronous results.md
problems/P-205-Graph-previews-must-rejec.title: P-205 — Graph previews must reject stale asynchronous results
problems/P-205-Graph-previews-must-rejec.content:
Status: resolved · Related: Rust Lossless Syntax and Patches
Problem
Graph locations describe indexed source, while an open document may contain unsaved edits. Parsing also finishes asynchronously, after a selection change, dismissal or document closure. Reusing an ordinal/range from an old snapshot can target another function.
Options























approachprosconsAApply indexed offsets after asynchronous parsinglittle statewrong-target and stale-edit riskBSnapshot-bound handles, review generations and document validationexplicit recoverable conflictsstale targets require fresh confirmation
Measurements
Native planner tests exercise exact-input handles, Unicode/CRLF edits, moves, invalid input, worker saturation and limits. The feature-enabled structural-edits browser suite drives actual graph selection through remote planning and normal editor history/save/conflict workflows. The handoff records final gate results.
Decision
B, behind the default-off structural-edits feature. Planning has no write path. Graph provenance may preselect only against matching input; recomputation requires confirming fresh functions. The existing document adapter alone commits edits. Two worker permits and raw/decoded input limits bound the server path.
Lesson
A graph selection, syntax handle, async response and editor session have distinct lifetimes. Preserve that distinction through preview and final application.

problems/P-206-Save-completion-must-ackn.filePath: problems/P-206 Save completion must acknowledge submitted text.md
problems/P-206-Save-completion-must-ackn.title: P-206 — Save completion must acknowledge submitted text
problems/P-206-Save-completion-must-ackn.content:
Status: resolved · Related: Rust Lossless Syntax and Patches
Problem
Workspace::save captured a text patch, awaited the source, then marked the current buffer as saved. Editing or undoing while that write was pending could make text that never reached the source appear clean. The recorded history character count also came from the newer buffer.
Options























approachprosconsALock editor input during savesimple acknowledgementblocks normal editingBAcknowledge the submitted text and versionnewer edits remain dirtyretain submitted text until completion
Measurements
The structural CodeMirror browser workflow exposed a save/undo timing race. A deterministic ext-api test holds the source apply future, edits the buffer, completes the save and verifies the submitted saved text/version and retained dirty newer text.
Decision
B. Save captures the submitted text alongside the patch, updates saved/version from that snapshot after success and records its character count. Conflicts retain the previous behavior. The browser workflow waits for canonical dirty state before saving and for successful acknowledgement before its next edit.
Lesson
Successful asynchronous persistence acknowledges the data sent, not whatever data is current when the response arrives.

problems/P-207-CodeMirror-external-edits.filePath: problems/P-207 CodeMirror external edits must preserve UTF-16 boundaries.md
problems/P-207-CodeMirror-external-edits.title: P-207 — CodeMirror external edits must preserve UTF-16 boundaries
problems/P-207-CodeMirror-external-edits.content:
Status: resolved · Related: Rust Lossless Syntax and Patches
Problem
CodeMirror’s external replacement diff compares UTF-16 code units. A common prefix or suffix could end inside a supplementary-plane character. Changing 𐐀 to 𐐁 produced from=4/to=5 with a lone low surrogate as the inserted text. Rust cannot deserialize that string or address that position as a scalar boundary, so its mirror could become stale.
Options























approachprosconsAReplace every byte on each Workspace updateavoids the splitloses useful minimal-diff selection mappingBWiden the changed region over surrogate pairs and CRLFvalid protocol and minimal surrounding changesexplicit boundary handling
Measurements
A direct probe of the committed CodeMirror bundle reproduced the lone-surrogate splice. The structural browser suite now checks both prefix and suffix surrogate boundaries and renames supplementary-plane Rust identifiers through the real graph, remote planner, editor and save path.
Decision
B. Workspace replacements remain one isolated undo entry; this also prevents a graph move from merging with recent user typing. The TypeScript source and rebuilt bundle are committed together.
Lesson
UTF-16 offsets and valid Unicode strings are separate requirements. A minimal diff must respect complete scalar values at both ends before crossing the Rust/JS boundary.

problems/P-208-Graph-rename-must-refuse-.filePath: problems/P-208 Graph rename must refuse incomplete file subsets.md
problems/P-208-Graph-rename-must-refuse-.title: P-208 — Graph rename must refuse incomplete file subsets
problems/P-208-Graph-rename-must-refuse-.content:
Status: resolved · Related: Rust Lossless Syntax and Patches
Problem
A graph-side declaration rename does not update references. Reusing LSP Rename
can return edits for several files, but the graph preview/undo contract currently
covers one document. Keeping only the origin’s edits would silently break callers.
Options





























approachprosconsAApply local subsetsmallincomplete refactoring, broken referencesBAccept complete single-file plans onlyexisting guarded history/previewrefuses multi-file renameCMulti-document proposalfull featureneeds explicit undo and partial-save policy
Measurements
Focused unit tests cover exact Unicode/CRLF plans and grouped history, URI aliases,
other-file and version-only targets, stale versions, duplicate/overlapping ranges,
surrogate boundaries, empty plans and budgets. The graph-rename browser suite uses
real rust-analyzer and both existing editor backends; final evidence is in the handoff.
Decision
Choose B for this slice. Check the complete LSP response before proposing edits;
reject any other-file target, unsupported resource edit or stale response. Keep
A unavailable. C remains future work. No autosave or new source transaction.
Lesson
A single-document preview may accept only a complete single-document refactoring.
The current document alone is insufficient for async freshness: also check the
server connection/version and open buffers used by the resolver.
2026-10-16 follow-up: option C is now implemented for complete plans within
one writable folder source, with coordinated history and separate per-file saves.
The incomplete-subset prohibition still holds. See
P-210 Multi-document rename needs coordinated history.

problems/P-209-CI-startup-stalls-must-re.filePath: problems/P-209 CI startup stalls must retain evidence.md
problems/P-209-CI-startup-stalls-must-re.title: P-209 — CI startup stalls must retain evidence
problems/P-209-CI-startup-stalls-must-re.content:
Status: resolved (startup recovery and evidence) · Related: Work Packages, Testing Strategy
Problem
Commit 5a4c012b’s structural browser CI job stalled for 1200 seconds without log
or target changes. Its final output was successful wasm-bindgen/esbuild installation,
not a compiler failure. The default browser job started from a restored cache.
The original cause is unproven. The screenshot-only artifact contained no files,
so the full startup log and owned process states were not archived.
Options





























approachprosconsAIncrease inactivity allowancesmallhides real hangs and loses evidenceBOne bounded stall retry plus diagnosticscan recover transient startup, preserves evidencea repeated stall still failsCUpgrade Dioxus speculativelymay change behaviorno established cause, broad change
Measurements
Failed run: github.com/MathStruct/Moonkale/actions/runs/38903191651
(job 116980223694). All other CI jobs passed. Local shell tests cover real isolated
process trees with fake time/HTTP: success, compiler failure, process exit,
one recovered stall, repeated stalls, a deadline shared between attempts,
default single attempt, and refusal/preservation of missing or mismatched process identity.
Decision
Choose B. CI explicitly requests noninteractive, verbose, locked startup. Default
local startup has one attempt; CI has two. Only inactivity retries, inside the
existing 3600-second total deadline; the 1200-second inactivity threshold is
unchanged. Each failed attempt records process/disk/progress diagnostics and
stops only its owned process group. Logs for both attempts survive a retry and
are uploaded with screenshots even after recovery. No environment/argument dump.
The original upstream stall is not claimed diagnosed by this infrastructure fix.
Lesson
A banner or tool-install message does not prove compilation began. Bound recovery,
retain the first failure, and keep compiler errors distinguishable from inactivity.

problems/P-210-Multi-document-rename-nee.filePath: problems/P-210 Multi-document rename needs coordinated history.md
problems/P-210-Multi-document-rename-nee.title: P-210 — Multi-document rename needs coordinated history
problems/P-210-Multi-document-rename-nee.content:
Status: resolved (experimental, default off) · Related: Rust Lossless Syntax and Patches, P-208 Graph rename must refuse incomplete file subsets
Problem
A complete rust-analyzer rename can span a declaration and consumers in several
files. Refusing the whole plan preserves safety but prevents this normal case.
Applying each file independently would leave a partial rename when one target
changes, and ordinary per-file undo would break the program again. Sources also
permit partial write success; buffer atomicity cannot promise disk atomicity.
Options





























approachprosconsAKeep refusing multi-file planssafe, simplecannot rename across modulesBStage complete buffers and coordinate marked history; save separatelysupports normal rename without overwriting newer editsneeds persistent view history and bounded preparationCRebase inverse patches over newer editsfewer blocked undossilently changes newer user work; complex conflict semantics
Measurements
Budgets: 64 files, 4096 edits, 4 MiB aggregate edit payload, 8 MiB combined
base/preview text; 512 KiB per-file input/output and 1 MiB per-file edits.
View preparation is limited to five seconds. Retained coordinated history is
bounded to 32 groups / 32 MiB. Browser probes use the committed CodeMirror bundle;
real rust-analyzer tests exercise the native and CodeMirror editors.
Decision
B. Two rename requests discover then authoritatively plan against prepared
same-folder buffers. A newly discovered target on the second response requires
Recompute. Immutable per-file proposals validate source/document/session/version
identity. All canonical edits/history are staged and assigned synchronously.
Ctrl+Z/Y, menu and review actions coordinate opaque history markers; newer edits
block the whole operation until their local history is restored. Document close,
backend change and bounded eviction retire the group, and old markers fail closed.
CodeMirror undo transactions bypass transaction filters (filter:false). Both
history probes and user commands therefore inspect the command’s dispatch
instead. Retain the opaque history field with its public initializer across
remounts: JSON serialization omits custom effects. Held views reject input, and
revision/sequence stamps discard queued stale messages. An authorized undo
briefly releases readOnly synchronously because CodeMirror otherwise refuses it.
Saving remains explicit and per file, continues after failure and records each
outcome. Successful writes are never rolled back automatically. Undo affects
buffers only, with dirty state relative to actual saved text.
Lesson
Multi-buffer edits require coordinated history ownership as well as staged text.
A framework’s filter is not necessarily on its history-command path; test the
actual bundled command protocol, including remounts, cancellation and redo.

problems/P-211-Preview-row-queries-and-f.filePath: problems/P-211 Preview row queries and folding repeated full text work.md
problems/P-211-Preview-row-queries-and-f.title: P-211 — Preview row queries and folding repeated full text work
problems/P-211-Preview-row-queries-and-f.content:
Status: resolved · Related: Rust Code Editor Implementation, Rust Code Editor Roadmap, Benchmarks
Problem
The unchanged live-preview-long typing bound failed on master 3b3f0fc5 and worsened after WP-69’s compact toolbar exposed more preview rows. Hiding the cursor word barely changed the profile. Restoring the toolbar’s old height reduced the workload: viewport geometry and the resulting preview updates mattered.
Measurements
Same isolated development server, Firefox, 247,882-byte Markdown note. Values are Preview / Source median milliseconds; no assertion is relaxed.








































RuntimePreview / SourceResultMaster 3b3f0fc5240.70 / 76.92failWP-69 7fd02ee0556.88 / 74.68failRow/folding/height fixes, original development profile125.58 / 72.26failIncluding the prose highlighting cache, original development profile84.50 / 75.36pass (p95 87.02 / 77.90)Final fresh-fixture code-only rerun, original development profile82.84 / 72.92pass (p95 86.14 / 76.20)Same final code, optional development profile overrides73.38 / 68.70pass (p95 77.76 / 70.66)
Separate Chromium CPU profiles with Wasm names identified repeated collapsed_rows line conversions, complete folding parses, and Markdown highlighting parses. Those diagnostic runs used a shortened navigation sequence; their absolute times are not interchangeable with the original Firefox suite. Development profile changes are measured separately and proposed as a separate commit; the code-only pass establishes the fix.
Decision
Resolve presentation endpoints against one scalar line-start table. Row-only and zero-cell visual queries use cached wrap boundaries without copying/scanning logical lines. Retain folding parser/tree state in a three-entry thread-local cache, with UTF-8-safe edits against the exact retained source.
Keep previous measured Markdown row heights as provisional estimates while a new revision is measured. Ownership, presentation, width and font epoch still gate estimates; input/caret geometry continues to require exact revision identity. Changed content is remeasured normally.
Markdown highlighting retains existing captures for ASCII alphanumeric appends at EOF only when the prefix matches exactly, the last nonempty line is at most 4096 bytes of plain ASCII prose, and no capture touches that tail. Syntax-changing, Unicode and earlier edits parse normally, including pending prose changes. Canonical source and independently derived structural folds remain current.
The migration test separately exposed SSR hydration: wait for the existing client /api/llm/info handshake before submitting Explorer, and guard transiently absent status bars.
Validation
Fresh-parser comparisons cover prose appends followed by syntax changes, Unicode, malformed fences, reference definitions and earlier edits that change context. Row-boundary tests cover indentation, Unicode, wrapping and folding. Browser coverage includes all 21 modified native suites plus 13 layout/geometry suites, and the 12 full-app suites; all pass on the code-only build. Final static checks and rustdoc pass without a Cargo patch. Workspace tests, Clippy, distribution checks and wasm are blocked by dioxus-code 0.1.2 build.rs writing to the read-only registry; Claude must rerun them outside the sandbox. The 206 code-view tests and workspace Clippy passed in preflight with an unchanged writable copy of that dependency. Per-suite results and retained evidence are in the handoff and commit request.
Lesson
A compact toolbar changes visible preview work. Profile the derived geometry and parsing before blaming a small label, and measure algorithm changes separately from compiler-profile changes.

problems/P-212-Markdown-offset-iterator-.filePath: problems/P-212 Markdown offset iterator can panic.md
problems/P-212-Markdown-offset-iterator-.title: P-212 — Markdown offset iterator can panic
problems/P-212-Markdown-offset-iterator-.content:
Status: resolved 2026-10-17 (Claude, after codex’s containment). The parser itself is fixed: Moonkale vendors pulldown-cmark 0.13.4 with upstream main’s one-hunk fix (edee73b7, pulldown-cmark #1129), substituted through [patch.crates-io] in the workspace and the fuzz crate, until 0.13.5 ships. Codex’s guard stays as a second layer. Related: Security, How to Write Tests, Work Packages.
Problem
CI run 39050073252, attempt 1, commit d58ad792, found a pulldown-cmark 0.13.4 panic in OffsetIter::next at parse.rs:2199. The saved artifact is 128 bytes (the initial handoff described 86). Arbitrary Markdown reaches this iterator through math, block preview, list/table/callout/image previews, wiki projection, heading lookup and documentation rendering. The native Properties front-matter recognizer does not use pulldown-cmark. Agent messages use plain iteration, which succeeds on this input; wiki snippets already reject NUL, but token exclusion did not.
Options





























approachprosconsAUpgrade the parserRemoves the upstream defect0.13.4 is still the latest published release on 2026-10-17BCatch failures at presentation boundariesKeeps canonical source; discards partial outputWorks only with unwinding; cannot recover from wasm release abortsCReject triggering control characters before parsing, plus BCovers this crash on abort profiles tooNUL/vertical-tab/form-feed documents retain plain source rather than formatted presentation
Measurements
A standalone stable harness compiling the original production math::displays from HEAD reproduces all four inputs. Stable Rust reproduces the original offset-iterator panic; plain iteration completes with 12 events. Greedy character deletion reaches nine bytes, Rust literal "- [\0]:[\n\u{b}". Replacing the NUL label with a still crashes, as does replacing the vertical tab with form feed: "- [a]:[\n\u{c}". Exhaustive single ASCII trailing-byte probes find vertical tab (11) and form feed (12); ordinary Unicode whitespace probes do not reproduce it. There is no YAML requirement.
Upstream #1129 already reports the same iterator bug. Its claim that NUL is required is narrower than the variants above. Releases offer no newer patch/minor; no dependency was changed.
Decision
Keep the original file bytes. Presentation boundaries reject NUL, vertical tab and form feed before parser construction, including on panic=abort wasm. On unwind builds, catch the whole parsing operation and discard partial output. Editor decoration providers return no decorations; hover becomes unavailable; documentation and agent messages retain literal text. Diagnostics contain fixed text only; rejected controls log once per process. No global panic hook is replaced.
The original crash and three minimized variants live in the math fuzz corpus and are normal stable regression fixtures across production entry points. The standalone fuzz target compiles the same production math parser and guard. This is containment for a known crash family, not a guarantee against every future parser defect in abort builds; upstream repair is still needed.
Follow-up (Claude, 2026-10-17)
The control-character skip did not cover the family: a 90-second local fuzz run found a tab-only input (p-212-tab.md), and the upstream issue already listed printable-only reproductions such as "- [o]:u\n    \t" (a whitespace-only line after a list item holding only a link reference definition). On the web client (panic=abort) these would still have crashed. So the root cause is now fixed in a vendored copy (packages/code-view/vendor/pulldown-cmark, see its MOONKALE_PATCHES.md; only src/firstpass.rs differs from the crate, and the WP-47 checksum manifest records it). markdown_guard::tests::patched_parser_survives_known_crash_inputs runs the parser unguarded on every known input with empty and all options; it fails at parse.rs:2199 on the unpatched source. A comment with the extra reproductions went to the upstream issue. Remove the vendored copy and the [patch.crates-io] entries when 0.13.5 or later ships with the fix; the control-character skip can go then too.
The next 3-minute fuzz run then found a second, smaller bug: the native math parser widened a display block back to its line start by searching for \n only, so with bare \r line endings (valid CommonMark) a block’s range reached back over the previous block, and the ranges overlapped. It now stops at \r too and never before the previous block’s end (native_math_parser::tests::bare_cr_lines_keep_ranges_ordered_and_disjoint, input p-212-overlap.md). After both fixes, 3,062,852 fuzz runs in 181 s found nothing.
Lesson
Minimization by deletion does not establish that a particular character value is necessary. Substitute ordinary labels and whitespace too. A catch boundary must surround lazy iterator consumption, and an abort-profile client needs prevention before parser construction.

problems/P-225-Native-FPS-recorder-miscl.filePath: problems/P-225 Native FPS recorder misclassifies idle cadence and input.md
problems/P-225-Native-FPS-recorder-miscl.title: P-225 — Native FPS recorder misclassifies idle cadence and input
problems/P-225-Native-FPS-recorder-miscl.content:
Status: resolved (recorder accounting; hardware rerun due) · Related: ADR-0023 Native editor frame measurements
Problem
Daniel’s 2026-10-21 KDE/NVIDIA/60 Hz recordings held 17–18 ms p95 and at most
48 ms, but idle medians of 8–11 ms classified ordinary frames as dropped.
Idle callback intervals alternate in pairs summing to about 16 ms. Held arrows
produced 91–112 keydowns with no repeat flags. Smooth scrolling produced many
viewport scroll events from only 3–4 larger wheel events; none met smallWheel.
Some 3 MB wheel attempts delivered wheel events but no viewport movement.
Options























approachprosconsAUpper-envelope idle calibration; count traversal and actual viewport movementHandles observed native delivery; keeps timing thresholds and rejects no-op gesturesScheduling estimate; physical presentation timing remains unmeasuredBRelax frame or interaction gatesNoneWould hide missed frames or missing gestures
Measurements
Raw reports remain read-only in ~/.cache/moonkale-fps-real/reports/{rust,threemb}.json.
The polluted rust.json[6] sample’s idle p95 is 15 ms rather than its 8 ms median.
The regression accepts 60 Hz gesture frames and rejects 32 ms frames. Clicking
Record and waiting four seconds on private sway/Mesa did not reproduce the
paired callbacks; precise KDE/NVIDIA scheduling cause remains unproven.
Nineteen clock/input regressions pass. Browser transport plus trusted arrow and
small-scroll checks pass using the current recorder against the existing panel
bundle. Fresh native source/preview/3 MiB runs validate six recorded interactions;
each arrow case observes 112 keys and each small-scroll case 63 viewport moves.
These observer-enabled development recordings are correctness evidence only.
Decision
Use idle p95, retain the ≥30 sample / ≤17 ms calibration guard and both existing
frame gates. Retain idle rAF deltas for follow-up. Count actual arrow inputs plus
caret/viewport change, independent of repeat. Count actual small viewport
movements on either axis with trusted wheel evidence. Ignore sink-only scrolls
and retain raw wheel axes/units and accumulated viewport travel. No-op 3 MB
wheel attempts still fail. See ADR-0023 Native editor frame measurements.
Lesson
Event flags and wheel deltas are backend-dependent. Observe the document’s
geometry as well as trusted events; callback cadence is not physical refresh.

problems/P-226-Real-desktop-FPS-host-und.filePath: problems/P-226 Real desktop FPS host undo report.md
problems/P-226-Real-desktop-FPS-host-und.title: P-226 — Real desktop FPS host undo report
problems/P-226-Real-desktop-FPS-host-und.content:
Status: resolved · Related: Rust Code Editor Roadmap
Problem
Daniel reported that typing in the release native FPS host followed by Ctrl+Z
did nothing. Synthetic renderer-probe undo already passed. The release binary
in ~/.cache/moonkale-fps-real must remain untouched.
Options























approachprosconsAReproduce with compositor keys and canonical text observationDistinguishes input delivery, focus and historyPrivate sway/Mesa differs from KDE/NVIDIABRemove workspace/session divergence reconciliationNone without evidenceRisks applying stale history over external edits
Measurements
A fresh native build on the private Wayland display receives trusted Ctrl+Z
(key=z, code=KeyZ, Ctrl set) and removes the final typed character, also
while recording. Native viewport key handling calls the same history callback
as shell Command::Undo, directly; it does not depend on shell dispatch.
The divergence guard is not reached for these ordinary local edits.
native-editor-fps-input.py now passes source, documentation preview and a
3 MiB single-line document: real typing, one-character undo/redo and selected
replacement undo all match exact canonical text. Its six native recorder
checks also pass interaction validation (112 arrow keys or 63 small viewport
movements per case). Reports are under target/next8/os-input*; these are
development correctness runs with observers, not FPS acceptance.
Cause
Cause (2026-10-22): Daniel’s KDE session had the US layout (~/.config/kxkbrc LayoutList=us, system layout de) on a German keyboard, so the key labelled Z sent Y and Ctrl+“Z” was redo. With the session on de, Ctrl+Z undoes (checked in Kate). Not an editor bug. The same mismatch made Daniel’s password fail on the lock screen (session layout) but not at login (system layout).
Decision
Keep the external-edit guard. Add an OS-input regression and opt-in FPS-host
canonical-text/passive-event observers to retain reproducible evidence. Do not
claim that Daniel’s real-session failure is fixed without reproducing it.
Lesson
A passing synthetic key test does not prove native delivery; a passing private
Wayland test likewise does not prove the user’s KDE session or keyboard layout.
A “shortcut does nothing” report from a real session: check the active keyboard layout against the physical keyboard first.

problems/P-227-Flow-code-generation-coul.filePath: problems/P-227 Flow code generation could not replace an existing file.md
problems/P-227-Flow-code-generation-coul.title: P-227 — Flow code generation could not replace an existing file
problems/P-227-Flow-code-generation-coul.content:
Status: resolved · Related: Flow Editor, Work Packages, Security
Problem
The first Generate created circuit.jl, but generating again after adding a
spring/mass left the old RC-only file intact. The panel passed the node listing’s
metadata version as the write precondition. Since WP-23, only a fetched content
version is a valid save precondition. The source correctly refused the stale token.
Options























approachprosconsAUse the fetched text and version togetherCorrect patch length and optimistic write preconditionOne content fetch, already requiredBRemove the preconditionNoneCould overwrite concurrent edits; rejected
Measurements
Reproduced by mtk.mjs’s second Generate (RC to mixed electrical/mechanical
model), 2026-10-23. The generated file retained 29 RC lines rather than the
40-line mixed golden. The first create and parameter editing succeeded.
Decision
The flow panel now fetches (text, version) and uses that version with the
whole-text patch derived from the same text. A failed fetch refuses the write;
there is no zero-length or metadata-version fallback. The existing MTK browser
regression checks the complete replacement byte-for-byte.
Lesson
Query/listing versions are freshness hints, not content write preconditions.
Keep fetched text, patch length and save version together.

problems/P-228-Pulse-browser-measurement.filePath: problems/P-228 Pulse browser measurement counted wraps as forward motion.md
problems/P-228-Pulse-browser-measurement.title: P-228 — Pulse browser measurement counted wraps as forward motion
problems/P-228-Pulse-browser-measurement.content:
Status: resolved · Related: Work Packages, How to Write Tests
Problem
graph-pulse.mjs took the largest absolute peak displacement across six pairs
of screenshots. A pulse wrapping from the end to the start of an edge could be
counted as a large forward displacement. Slow and fast pulses were also sampled
in separate captures/time windows, so their maxima did not measure comparable
speeds. The existing shader uses periodic forward motion; no pulse renderer
behavior changed in WP-04.
Options























approachprosconsASample both edges in shared frames, reject wraps and compare velocitiesMeasures the intended behavior and retains speed/LOD assertionsMore profile samplesBRetry until a favorable phase passesNoneWould hide the measurement error; rejected
Measurements
Observed in NEXT-11 on 2026-10-23, including a run holding the bench lock and both
heavy slots: the old test reported slow 63 px versus fast 36 px. An earlier run
passed with the same renderer. Absolute maxima across phase wraps are not speed.
Decision
The fixture now pins equal-length edges. Thirteen shared captures sample both
brightness profiles at finer resolution. Boundary/off-stroke peaks and backward
wrap intervals are excluded; median forward screen velocities are checked
against each declared speed and the 3:1 ratio. The zoomed-out animation LOD check
remains. No renderer pulse behavior or numerical speed is changed.
Lesson
Periodic motion needs directed, wrap-aware measurements over shared intervals.
A maximum absolute displacement is neither an unwrapped distance nor a velocity.

problems/P-229-Sophia-full-graph-travers.filePath: problems/P-229 Sophia full graph traversal can exhaust its worker stack.md
problems/P-229-Sophia-full-graph-travers.title: P-229 — Sophia full graph traversal can exhaust its worker stack
problems/P-229-Sophia-full-graph-travers.content:
Status: resolved (Sophia bed1e02e, 2026-10-23) · Related: Case Selector, Graph View, Problem Log P-224
Problem
The first coarse-query experiment delegated to SophiaSource::query(All) with
an expanded two-million-node cap. On the disposable copy of the P-224 generated
100k-name store (target/next9/gen100000.sophia, 649 MiB), the Tokio blocking
worker exhausted its stack and aborted before returning a graph. The previous
100k cap kept most definition records outside the returned slice. Increasing
that cap reached code paths the earlier measurement did not exercise.
The pinned Sophia interface’s all enumerates names and records and calls
edges_at for definition nodes. That path calls definition_of and recursively
walks terms to infer Calls. The abort was observed inside the worker; no native
stack trace establishes the exact overflowing frame, so that causal detail is
an inference from the implementation, not a measured backtrace.
Options





























approachprosconsARaise the worker stackeasy experimentdoes not establish a traversal boundBCoarse queries use namespace/name/id/indexed-reference metadatano term decode, fits the coarse navigation purposedoes not infer Calls; full traversal still needs an upstream fixCBound/rewrite Sophia term decoding/walksfixes the underlying traversalrequires a separate Sophia change/tag and regression fixture
Measurements
Native development profile, pinned Sophia rev 4c2aaab, disposable store copy:

Initial full-snapshot attempt: worker stack overflow and process abort;
target/coarse-sophia-copy.log.
Metadata-only coarse path: 199,257 input nodes → 2 representatives, zero
projected cross-region edges; 3,682.8 ms cold, then 1,826.3 / 1,811.6 ms.
target/coarse-sophia-copy-fixed.log.
Existing public sample-store tests still verify namespace members, complete
root counts and shared-definition ownership. The generated store remains a
local reproduction; no 649 MiB binary is added to the repository.

Decision
Use B for WP-06: read metadata on the blocking worker, preserve real namespace
Contains/Names and indexed References, assign shared definitions to one stable
name for navigation, then run the bounded shared projection. Check the store log
position before/after metadata listing and refuse a changed snapshot. Coarse
navigation does not infer Calls or load definition bodies. No stack-size change,
dependency update or upstream modification is made.
The original All/neighbour/body paths are not declared fixed. An upstream
bounded traversal plus a small hermetic stored-term regression remains open.
The cold copied-store query also exceeds two seconds; source-native cached
cuts remain an optimization task. The synthetic source-native browser acceptance
is measured separately and does not hide this limit.
Lesson
A hierarchy summary must not require decoding every term in the source. Prefer
indexed relations and metadata; increasing a presentation cap can reach dormant
recursive paths even when the final visible graph is tiny.
Resolution (2026-10-23)
Fixed upstream in Sophia bed1e02e, now pinned. sophia-89 reproduced it: in a debug build, decoding and walking every record of gen100000 on a 2 MiB thread overflows (the deepest record nests 700 encoded levels; a release build doesn’t). Calls edges now come from sophialang_core::encode::called_refs, which reads the stored bytes with an explicit stack and builds no terms (same 240 011 calls on all 99 254 definitions; a 20 000-deep definition scans on a 64 KiB stack). A second problem was quadratic edge de-duplication (Vec::contains over 739 000 edges); it is a hash set now. all(2_000_000) on a copy of gen100000 on a 2 MiB thread: 199 256 nodes and 739 273 edges in 2.6 s (release), 14.9 s (debug). The coarse path keeps reading metadata only.
Still recursive on Sophia’s side: fetch_text (decode and print) of those deep generated definitions; in a debug build on a 2 MiB worker, opening one of them could still overflow. SP-015 (bounding depth at store time) is the real fix; a larger Tokio thread_stack_size would cover it until then.

problems/P-231-Sophia-folder-replay-lose.filePath: problems/P-231 Sophia folder replay loses generic memberships.md
problems/P-231-Sophia-folder-replay-lose.title: P-231 — Sophia folder replay loses generic memberships
problems/P-231-Sophia-folder-replay-lose.content:
Status: resolved upstream (Sophia 77f5c1c9; pinned by rev until the v0.1.1 tag) · Related: Indexing, ADR-0029 Sophia stores the code graph
Problem
A replay of Lenticulum.jl’s real history against Sophia v0.1.0 produces live
names/memberships that disagree with a fresh build of the same tree, even when
the per-file manifests agree. The gate cannot pass with lost or stale facts.
Store::replace_files deduplicates new generic members by content digest but
subtracts every entry in an old manifest’s member list. Two methods can have
the same normalized identity. Refreshing their file can therefore subtract two
contributions after adding only one, retracting a method that is still present.
The old manifest retains both entries. This is a Sophia-side accounting bug.
Options























approachprosconsADeduplicate old contributions in Sophia, per file/generic/digestMatches new contribution accountingRequires a new upstream release and replayBRewrite/repair the cache during measurementNone for this gateHides the error and invalidates equivalence evidence
Measurements
See Indexing for the full histories, checkpoint differences and timings.
The minimal ignored regression is
packages/services/index/tests/history_replay.rs::repeated_generic_content_survives_a_file_refresh.
It adds f(x::Int) = x and f(y::Int) = y, then adds a comment and refreshes.
Both commits should equal a fresh store; v0.1.0 loses the generic on refresh.
Decision
Request the Sophia fix, keep the failure visible, and leave gate 4 unmet.
No upstream checkout or replayed repository is modified. The exact request
and reproduction command are in the untracked HANDOFF-from-codex.md.
Review generic-to-content transitions too: their old nominal relations can be
left orphaned when generic delta processing sees a Content target and skips it.
Lesson
File manifests are necessary evidence, but are not sufficient: compare actual
names and live memberships, and enumerate facts on historical subjects too.
Resolution (2026-10-24)
Sophia 77f5c1c9 fixes two causes. (1) Old and new contributions are both
counted once per (file, generic). (2) Names changing kind: a generic that becomes
a definition closes its old nominal relations in the same batch, and a freed name
rebuilds its memberships from every file’s manifest. Sophia added replay
regressions on all four backends. Moonkale pins the rev, the regression
repeated_generic_content_survives_a_file_refresh runs again, and both history
replays are clean (Indexing). Stores written by v0.1.0 may hold wrong counts:
delete .moonkale/code.sophia to rebuild.

A normal retry reuses the complete archive and retains symbol localization; upstream metadata destination remains open.openWP-03 M5 build evidenceP-200 Lazy syntactic content identitiesDefault-off explicit Rust/Julia/Python normalization, canonical recursive components, exact-input freshness and bounded memory/optional persistent caches; conservative syntax failures remain explicit.resolved (experimental v1)WP-66P-201 Workspace settings “not saved: version conflict” on the first start with a state storeSeen on Android (2026-10-15) and reproduced in a test: the one-off layout migration saves the folder’s .moonkale/settings.json twice in quick succession. The saves overlapped: the second expected a version the first had replaced (the error), and in other interleavings the older snapshot overwrote the newer change or, through the folder source’s (mtime, len) versions, replaced only part of the file. Writes of the folder settings file now never overlap (a gate in SettingsState: a save during a write asks for one more run), each run builds the text from the current state and writes against the version it just read, and an unchanged file is not rewritten. Test: ext-api/tests/state_layout_overlap.rs.resolved—P-202 Lossless edits must conserve syntax tokensError-free parses could lose code after an EOF-comment move. The default-off Rust planner now preserves function count and the complete terminal token inventory, rejects unsafe placements, validates names and checks final output size.resolvedWP-67 slice 1P-203 Nested browser fixtures cannot load in rust-analyzerFixtures under target inherited Moonkale’s workspace and failed Cargo metadata, so lsp2 never received diagnostics. Generated fixture manifests now include an empty workspace table; assertions/timeouts unchanged.resolvedWP-67 verification
| P-204 Structural proposals must retain document identity | A syntax hash alone cannot guard editor history, close/reopen, source replacement or source-version changes. Bounded Workspace proposals now check these identities and revisions, preserve previews on conflict and use ordinary undo/save paths. | resolved | WP-67 slice 2 |
| P-205 Graph previews must reject stale asynchronous results | Experimental graph reviews use snapshot-bound handles, request generations and non-mutating document validation. Stale work cannot apply; conflicts retain previews and require fresh selection/recomputation. | resolved | WP-67 slice 3 |
| P-206 Save completion must acknowledge submitted text | A save could acknowledge edits made after its source write began and incorrectly clear dirty state. Completion now records the submitted snapshot and its character count; newer edits stay dirty. | resolved | WP-67 integration |
| P-207 CodeMirror external edits must preserve UTF-16 boundaries | The common-prefix/suffix replacement could emit a lone surrogate for supplementary-plane identifier changes. External diffs now widen over whole UTF-16 pairs, in addition to CRLF, and remain isolated undo entries. | resolved | WP-67 integration |
| P-208 Graph rename must refuse incomplete file subsets | Reference-aware graph Rename accepts complete single-file LSP plans and refuses multi-file plans in full. Resolver inputs and connection versions stay guarded through preview and Apply. | resolved | WP-67 slice 4 |
| P-209 CI startup stalls must retain evidence | CI now keeps per-attempt startup logs/process diagnostics and permits one inactivity-only retry inside the original deadline. Owned process-group cleanup covers compiler/server descendants; compiler failures and process exits do not retry. Original tooling-stage stall remains unproven. | resolved (recovery/evidence) | WP-26 |
| P-210 Multi-document rename needs coordinated history | Two-pass complete same-folder rename plans stage all buffers, coordinate marked native/CodeMirror history and save explicitly per file with partial-success results. Newer edits block all-file undo; history probes and menu/keyboard commands guard CodeMirror dispatch, including remounts and held input. | resolved (experimental) | WP-67 slice 5 |
| P-211 Preview row queries and folding repeated full text work | Typing in the Rust editor’s Markdown preview was slow on long documents (live-preview-long: 234 ms per keystroke on master, 534 ms after the WP-69 toolbar exposed more rows, against Source at 73 ms). Row lookups rescanned rope text per token, folding reparsed the whole text, and highlighting reparsed on every append. Now one line-start table per presentation pass, row-only boundary queries, a bounded per-thread folding parse cache, provisional measured Markdown row heights, and reuse of highlight captures for plain ASCII appends at the end of an unhighlighted line; 83 ms against 73 in a dev build. Typing mid-document still reparses highlighting in full. | resolved | WP-69 |
| P-212 Markdown offset iterator can panic | The first CI math fuzz crash reaches production Markdown offset iterators. NUL/vertical-tab/form-feed inputs now retain plain source before parser construction on all profiles; unwind builds discard complete failed parses. Original and minimized inputs cover production entry points. 216 code-view and five agent tests pass with the supported registry-write bypass; browser gates remain due; upstream #1129 remains open. Root cause fixed: a vendored pulldown-cmark 0.13.4 with upstream’s one-hunk fix (#1129) until 0.13.5. | resolved | WP-47 |
| P-213 A clean Windows machine cannot build the desktop app without LLVM and Perl | First Windows source build (a friend’s Windows 10 PC, 2026-10-17): the portable crates and moonkale-remote --lib pass, but cargo test --workspace and dx serve stop in librocksdb-sys’s build script — bindgen finds no libclang.dll. moonkale-desktop (and moonkale-server’s kv feature) enable moonkale-sources-kv with rocksdb unconditionally. CI and the Windows release job pass only because GitHub’s windows-latest image ships LLVM. With LLVM installed the build then stops in openssl-sys (vendored on Windows, P-125): OpenSSL’s Configure needs a native Perl (Strawberry Perl). Documented in Install (install LLVM, set LIBCLANG_PATH, install Strawberry Perl); dropping OpenSSL on Windows depends on P-125, and making RocksDB an optional desktop feature would change what the Windows build opens and is left open | documented | — |
| P-214 On Windows the window opened under a top taskbar and taller than the screen | First Windows GUI run (2026-10-17, 1920×1080 at 125 %, taskbar docked at the top): the undecorated window opened at y = 0 and 1400×900 logical, so our own title bar sat under the taskbar (no drag, no double-click) and the status bar ran off the bottom. fit_to_work_area (desktop main.rs) now moves and shrinks each new window into its monitor’s work area (MonitorFromWindow/GetMonitorInfoW); the clamp is fit_rect, unit-tested on Linux; the Windows call type-checks against tao for MSVC. Confirmed on the Windows PC (2026-10-17): fitted (128, 0, 1896, 1102) into (0, 38, 1920, 1080); title bar reachable and draggable, status bar visible | resolved | — |
| P-215 The palettes and dialogs drew without a background | Found on Windows (2026-10-17) through the WebView2 devtools: Ctrl+P and Ctrl+Shift+P are children of .mk-frame, outside .wb-shell, and the --wb-* variables were only declared on .wb-shell/.wb-workspace — background: var(--wb-surface) resolved to nothing, so the list was drawn transparently over the editor. Not Windows-specific. theme::builtin_css now declares them on .mk-frame too; unit test; confirmed on Windows (both palettes solid). The CodeMirror find bar is a separate problem (P-219) | resolved | spec 030 |
| P-216 An oversized graph canvas panicked the renderer | Found on Windows (2026-10-17): a restored graph tab measured 1750×27197 device px before layout; Surface::configure panicked past the 16384 texture limit and every later call hit RefCell already borrowed. fit_texture clamps the surface to the device’s max_texture_dimension_2d (and zero to one). Confirmed on Windows: a restored graph tab renders, no panic. Why the canvas measured 27197 px is not known | resolved | spec 031 |
| P-217 Minimise and restore brought another tab to the front | Windows (2026-10-17): Graph was replaced by the last document after a tiny minimised viewport switched phone/wide layouts. Fixed 2026-10-22: shell document activation is a navigation edge retained outside the remounted workbench; each layout keeps its active tabs. Ignore viewport dimensions below 100 px, and observe both resize and media-query changes. VirtualDom checks Graph and Search selections across two round trips; browser responsive-tabs checks the real shell. Packaged Linux/WebKit desktop retains Graph across 1600 → 420 → 1600 px output resizing. Windows minimise/restore recheck remains | fixed locally; Windows recheck | — |
| P-218 Rich view resolved relative images against the app, not the folder | Windows (2026-10-17): README image requested from the app origin and failed. Fixed 2026-10-22: display-only Milkdown image node views ask Rust for source-backed data URLs through the existing native-preview source jail, byte/pixel limits, freshness checks and bounded cache. Original Markdown destinations survive editing/save; escaping and remote paths receive no URL. Browser rich-images checks a percent-encoded subfolder image (240 × 80), blocked destinations and saved paths. Packaged Linux/WebKit desktop also displays the 240 × 80 subfolder SVG. Windows recheck remains | fixed locally; Windows recheck | — |
| P-219 The CodeMirror find bar is unstyled | Windows (2026-10-17): native inputs/buttons/checkboxes and English in the German UI. Fixed 2026-10-22: search controls use shell colour tokens and EditorState phrases from en/de/zh-CN locale tables; generated bundle rebuilt from TypeScript. Browser codemirror-search opens the actual German panel, checks input/button styling and selects a match. Packaged Linux/WebKit desktop shows the same styled German controls. Windows recheck remains | fixed locally; Windows recheck | — |
| P-220 graph-rename sometimes waits in vain for rust-analyzer’s first diagnostic | CI browser structural edits, twice on 2026-10-18 (runs 39081507412 on a docs-only commit and 39126973008): the first step times out after 120 s on .cm-lint-marker-error (CodeMirror) — rust-analyzer never published the expected error. The commit before passed with the same toolchain, and the rerun of 39126973008 passed: flaky, cause unknown (a cold rust-analyzer on a shared runner, or a lost first publishDiagnostics). If it recurs, log the LSP traffic of that step | open | — |
| P-221 The release web client failed to bundle on Rust 1.99 | Release 261019-proto (2026-10-19): the Linux and Arch jobs stopped at wasm-bindgen error: the __wasm_bindgen_unstable custom section is missing, but the module still contains wasm-bindgen shims; Windows, macOS, Android and Nix (no web client) built. Reproduced locally with 1.99.1 and not with 1.98.1 (same wasm-bindgen 0.2.128): strip = true in [profile.wasm-release] makes dx strip everything, which now includes that section. strip = "debuginfo" builds on 1.99.1; the module is the same size (49.2 MB vs 49.3 MB). CI never builds the release web client, so nothing caught it before a tag | resolved | — |
| P-222 The desktop graph panel drew nothing (WebKitGTK 2.54) | Found in the Sophia desktop check (2026-10-21): the graph toolbar said 5106 nodes · 6915 edges · gl, but the canvas stayed empty, for folders too, on Daniel’s NVIDIA desktop and on the headless display. Chromium and MiniBrowser (WebKitGTK 2.54.1) drew the web build. The cause is dioxus-desktop’s Wayland workaround: it sets WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1 and GDK_BACKEND=x11 for WebKit’s children, and since WebKitGTK 2.54 (installed 2026-10-08) a WebGL canvas stays blank with the DMA-BUF renderer off (the headless app with only that variable draws nothing; without it, it draws). Native Wayland with the DMA-BUF renderer then failed on NVIDIA with GTK’s “Error 71 (Protocol error)”; __NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1 avoids it. Fix: desktop/main.rs turns the workaround off (with_disable_dma_buf_on_wayland(false)) and sets __NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC=1 on Wayland when the NVIDIA driver is loaded; MOONKALE_WEBKIT_X11=1 restores the old behaviour. Verified: LinearAlgebra’s 5106 nodes and the 100 000-node store draw on Daniel’s desktop, the m2root fixture on the headless display | resolved | 16 |
| P-223 Zoomed far out, dragging the graph moves a node instead of panning | Daniel, 100 000-node Sophia store (2026-10-21): far out, nearly every point of the canvas is within a node’s pick radius, so a drag picks a node and moves it. Panning is only possible between nodes. Candidates: a pick radius that shrinks with the drawn node size, or a press that pans when the node is smaller than a few pixels; fixed 2026-10-22: overview dots below 3 CSS px radius stay clickable but drag the camera, with projected 3D/shape sizes respected. Dense 10k-node pointer regression fails the old wasm and passes the rebuilt engine; normal node dragging remains covered | resolved | 16 |
| P-224 The 100 000-node graph takes about 15 s to appear | Measured 2026-10-22 on a copied store, actual desktop desktop,sophia, private 1920×1080 Wayland/WebKit/Mesa software GL, bench lock + both slots: initial query-to-first-draw 6.78 → 2.54 s, five warm loads median 5.70 → 2.63 s, worst 5.93 → 2.69 s; graph visible in a compositor screenshot at 2.7 s. Initial source query 3.89 → 1.39 s, payload 96 → 93 ms, eval handoff 2.26 → 0.72 s, stringify 14 → 0 ms, engine parse/build/fit/layout/draw 518 → 341 ms (layout now follows the first draw). Actual panel JSON is 14.2 MB; 50 MB was the whole source result. Fixes: watcher snapshots log tail instead of replaying history, edge ids reused, duplicate in-flight reads coalesced with freshness guards, development query optimization, JSON-string eval transport, no property clones and draw before layout. Isolated browser engine median 309 → 114 ms; graph-startup checks pixels and the zero-step first frame. Full method/raw artifact names in packages/graph-render/graph-render.md. Original 15 s not reproduced here; physical NVIDIA/KDE recheck remains | fixed locally; desktop recheck | 16 |
| P-225 Native FPS recorder misclassifies idle cadence and input | Upper-envelope idle calibration, backend-independent arrow traversal evidence and actual small document scroll movements; timing thresholds unchanged, no-op wheel attempts still fail. Precise paired-callback scheduling cause and hardware rerun remain open. | resolved (accounting) | WP-02 |
| P-226 Real desktop FPS host undo report | Real compositor Ctrl+Z works in a fresh private-display FPS host, including while recording; add canonical-text/input observations and OS regression. Cause (2026-10-22): Daniel’s KDE session had the US layout (~/.config/kxkbrc LayoutList=us, system layout de) on a German keyboard, so the key labelled Z sent Y and Ctrl+“Z” was redo. With the session on de, Ctrl+Z undoes (checked in Kate). Not an editor bug. | resolved | WP-02 |
| P-227 Flow code generation could not replace an existing file | Second Generate retained the old RC-only circuit.jl: the flow panel used a listing metadata version instead of its fetched content version. It now uses fetched text/version together and refuses failed fetches. The MTK second-generation golden is the browser regression (2026-10-23). | resolved | WP-05 |
| P-228 Pulse browser measurement counted wraps as forward motion | The pulse suite compared maxima of absolute peak movement in separate screenshots, counting phase wraps as speed. It now samples both edges in shared frames, rejects wrap/boundary pairs and checks median forward velocities against declared speeds. Renderer pulse behavior is unchanged (2026-10-23). | resolved | WP-04 |
| P-229 Sophia full graph traversal can exhaust its worker stack | Increasing All to materialise a complete coarse snapshot reached a worker stack overflow on the P-224 copied store. Coarse navigation now reads namespace/name/definition-ID/indexed-reference metadata, without decoding terms; 199,257 nodes → 2 representatives in 3.68 s cold / 1.81–1.83 s warm. Original full traversal: fixed upstream in Sophia bed1e02e (Calls without term recursion, edges de-duplicated by set): all(2 000 000) on a gen100000 copy, 199 256 nodes / 739 273 edges in 2.6 s release. | resolved | WP-06 |
| P-230 macOS watch tests see the fixture’s own writes | CI Portable macos-14 (advisory) failed twice in 25 master runs on project-fs watch tests: run 39889363844 an_unknown_position_asks_for_a_reset_and_an_idle_poll_returns_empty (the idle poll returned 2 paths, the fixture’s src/main.rs and README.md) and run 39483652408 ignores_hidden_gitignored_and_temporary_files. FSEvents delivered the fixture’s writes after the watcher had started. Fix: the test fixture waits 1.5 s on macOS before the source opens. Linux and Windows unchanged | resolved | — |
| P-231 Sophia folder replay loses generic memberships | ADR-0029 history replay finds live generic names/members differing from fresh stores; Sophia v0.1.0 subtracts duplicate old member digests without the deduplication used for new contributions. Fixed in Sophia 77f5c1c9; both replays clean | resolved | — |
Conventions

Status: open · investigating · decided · resolved · wontfix.
Link the ADR if the resolution became a decision.
Include measurements, not adjectives (“30 fps at 50k nodes on WebGL2”, not “slow”).

The problems foreseen before building, ranked. Difficulty 1–5 (effort + unknowns); Risk = how much else breaks if it goes wrong. Problems actually hit while building are logged in the Problem Log as P-nnn; what is being worked on next is the Roadmap; the current state per area is Status.


                  
                  Two id spaces 
                  
                

Until 2026-10-01 these rows were numbered P-01 … P-35, which collided with the Problem Log’s P-032 … P-035 (P-32 “git” here, P-032 “release-build observability” there). The ranking now uses R-nn everywhere in the vault; the log keeps P-nnn.

Reading the table

What is left of the original top risks: R-01 (the model’s missing half), R-05 (the extension API’s missing half), R-16, R-20 and R-22. R-36 and R-37 are new and have the widest blast radius — every crate touches the state and the Workspace.
R-37 and R-39 come before new features: they are what makes the rest cheap to change. R-38 comes before any server is exposed beyond a trusted network.
Anything marked research has no committed date.

problems/Roadmap.title: Roadmap
problems/Roadmap.content:
Where things stand today is Status; the anticipated hard problems and their state are the Problem Ranking (R-nn). This page is the order; the open work cut into parallel packages for several agents is Work Packages, and the direction behind it is the North Star.
Next





















































#whatwhy nowdepends on1Milestone 18 - Library Refactor phases 0–4: CI, pruning, layering, the Workspace as services, the catalogue out of the shell, server contributionsevery later feature is cheaper and safer after it; CI first (R-39)—2State interface (stable for redb) → internal-store comparison → ADR-0014 One store for internal state accepted → refactor phase 5announced by Daniel after Milestone 17; settings, history, sessions, projects and a persisted index all wait for it (R-36)1 (phase 3 makes the services it plugs into)—Local fixes from the audit: #2, #6, #9, #11, #12, #15 done on dev-claude (2026-10-04, Audit 2026-09-23); left: #5, #10, #14, close #16small, independentnothing; any time3Writes to database sources (R-41)every source is read-only today; announced after Milestone 171 (openers, classifier on the source)4Projects (R-40, Projects and Sources, spec 003)cross-source links (R-16), per-source colour and read-only, sync2 (projects live in the store)5The Lenticulum path (Julia and Lenticulum): flow editor with undirected ports and nested subgraphs → MTK library → a live graph source and the factor-graph viewerthe reason Moonkale exists1 (graph renderer as a library, moonkale-julia repo)6Graph coarse tier (Case Selector) and the plain-text tierfactor graphs and code graphs past 100k nodes1
Candidates, documented and not ordered yet: Unicode Input (spec 004), Markdown Diagrams and Math (fence renderers), Annotations, Notebook Editor, Publishing Sources (reader mode), Collaboration (CRDT editing), accounts and roles for a shared server (Remote and Server Modes), the Julia depot as a read-only source, specs 024/025 (go to definition from the cursor, five-button mouse), spec 028 (phone vault export, Storage Access Framework), the remaining JS → Rust replacements (JavaScript Inventory), Postgres/Redis/TypeDB/FalkorDB sources.
